To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the parton fragmentation within an jet can be calculated in a systematic expansion in powers of αs, and that the logarithmic terms that appear in the expansion can be resummed in a perturbation series.
the fragmentation function for a light hadron in a light jet is the product of a jet function and the standard fragmentation function, and that we have computed this product to NNLL accuracy.

the oneloop coefficients for the matching of the fragmenting quark and gluons jet functions to the standard fragmentation functions are finite and that these coefficients can have a large effect on the extraction of fragmentation functions from dijet + h data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of parton fragmentation within an jet at NNLL accuracy.

the study of the parton fragmentation within an energetic jet, where we calculate the oneloops coefficients of the corresponding jet functions, and apply our results to the extraction of the fragmentation functions.
the study of the fragmentation of a parton i into a hadron h within an energetic jet.

the NNLO jet functions are known, and the NLO matching coefficients for the fragmenting jet function are known.

the matching coefficients for fragmenting jet functions are calculable and can be used to improve the extraction of fragmentation functions from dijet + h data.
